To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genes aglB and Ag1A, coding for the enzymes of starch degradation, were isolated from Thermotoga neopolita and subcloned into expression vectors.

the recombinant enzymes AglB and AGLA, produced by E. coli, hydrolyse starch, maltodextrins, and cyclodextrins to their monomers, and the recombinant proteins can serve as a basis for the development of new biotechnological applications in food and pharmaceutical industries, and in the production of biofuels and biodegradable plastics.
the genes aglB and glaA from the starch/maltooligosaccharide utilization gene cluster of the hyperthermophilic archaeon Thermotoga neopolita were cloned and expressed in Escherichiacoli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning of the genes of the starch utilization cluster from T. neapolitana and with the expression and characterization of the recombinant proteins.

the characterization of the first hyperthermostable alpha-glucoside hydrolases with a wide action spectrum, and it is the first report of an enzyme that is able to hydrolyse alpha-galactosides with a high efficiency.

the first description of enzymes from the family of hyperthermostable alpha-glucosyltransferases, and the results of this study are of importance for the development of biotechnological methods for starch hydrolysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzyme AglB is a novel type of cyclodextrin-glucanotransferase with a unique mode of action.
the two recombinant enzymes are hyperthermophilic alpha-glucosylhydrolases with different specificities, but with similar properties.
AglB is a cyclodextinase with alpha-amylase activity, and AglA is an alpha-glucoside hydrolase with alpha-amlyase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enzymes of T. neapolitana are able to hydrolyse all the intermediate products of degradation of starch and its derivatives, including the products of hydrolysis of cyclodextrins.
AglB hydrolyses alpha-glycosidic bonds in oligoglucoside and oligogalactoside chains from the non-reduced end of the molecule.

the genes of the starch/maltotetradextrin utilization cluster of T. neapolitana encode enzymes with a broad range of action and substrate specificity, capable of hydrolysis of a wide range of oligosaccharides and disaccharides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enzymes of the agl gene cluster from T. neapolitana are hyperthermostables, which are capable of degrading starch and maltodextrans to glucose and maltodextrin.
the enzymes of the Thermotoga neopolitan gene cluster are hyperthermostabilized homologues of enzymes of the glycoside hydrolase family 13, and they have unique properties.
the enzymes of the T. neapolitana starch degradation pathway have unique substrate specificity and catalytic properties.
